title: eMudhra intermediate CA key compromise — clients still trusting the eight compromised intermediates

real_sca_status_legend.caught_by_feed: A package-level CVE/advisory exists; a CVE-keyed SCA feed matches the vulnerable version range.
real_sca_status_legend.blind_no_advisory: No package CVE was issued; remediated by a trust-bundle content update. CVE-keyed SCA feeds have nothing to match, so they miss it.
real_sca_status_legend.blind_toolchain_unresolved: A CVE exists, but it lives in the language stdlib/toolchain, which manifest-based SCA does not resolve as a package (observed: go.mod -> 0 packages).

rules.note: Any 1.27.x<1.27.3, 1.26.x<1.26.10, or <=1.25.x still accepts a chain containing one of the eight keys. CVE exists, but go.mod resolves to 0 packages in real SCA — the toolchain is not a resolved dependency.

2026.10.19 drops emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from the bundle. No certifi CVE was issued for eMudhra; Python treats it as a bundle update (GHSA only). CVE-keyed SCA shows 0 risk on any certifi version for this incident.
Excludes emSign ECC Root CA - G3, emSign Root TLS CA - G3 and AAA Certificate Services by public key. Bundle content update, not a package CVE.
OneCRL / NSS trusted-cert list update. No eMudhra package CVE against nss confirmed; distro advisories wrap the bundle change, not a code flaw.

pending_confirmation.reason: patched versions available, exact boundary unconfirmed
